submission.natural_language_explanation: This head fires retrospectively on tokens that immediately continue a stereotyped boilerplate/template frame -- license and copyright scaffolds ('Use of this source code is governed by ...', 'Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation under ...', 'WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either ...') and fixed legal formulae ('except for establishing [res judicata]') -- with peak attention weight near 1.0 on an anchor word 1-4 tokens back inside the frame (OV circuit suppresses rather than copies, copying score -0.66; previous-token 0.29, duplicate/induction ~0). Rewording the frame while keeping its meaning strongly reduces firing, replacing only the words after the peak leaves firing unchanged, and isolated novel prose or ordinary code stays below the line.

rival_explanations: It is a generic previous-token and syntactic-dependency head that fires on any predictable dependent (noun after 'of', verb after 'that') in all prose, with boilerplate merely its strongest case -- predicts isolated ordinary sentences fire, contrary to measurements where all sit below ~0.21x max.

It is a lookahead head that fires to predict the specific upcoming boilerplate token (e.g. 'res' predicts 'judicata'), so changing the tail after the peak should change firing -- predicts the pizza-recipes tail swap drops activation, contrary to the measured zero delta.
